drivingQuestion: Is the one who recites the blessing greater than the one who answers amen, and after whose blessing does one answer amen?
outcomeNote: Each difficulty is answered: the mishna's amen is that of one who did not eat with the company; the ranking of blesser and answerer is a tannaitic dispute; Rav rules on schoolchildren. The baraita's dispute over oil is left standing, with Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak grounding the practice in Leviticus 20:26 instead.

segments.he: לְמֵימְרָא דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא שָׁמַע כּוּלָּהּ בְּרָכָה עוֹנֶה? וְכִי לָא שָׁמַע הֵיכִי נָפֵיק?
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «Is that to say that» if «a Jew» recites a blessing, «even though one did not hear the entire blessing, he responds» amen? «If he did not hear» the entire blessing, «how did he fulfill» his obligation?

segments.he: אָמַר חִיָּיא בַּר רַב: בְּשֶׁלֹּא אָכַל עִמָּהֶן, וְכֵן אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ בְּשֶׁלֹּא אָכַל עִמָּהֶן. אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב לְחִיָּיא בְּרֵיהּ: בְּרִי, חֲטוֹף וּבָרֵיךְ. וְכֵן אֲמַר רַב הוּנָא לְרַבָּה בְּרֵיהּ: חֲטוֹף וּבָרֵיךְ.
segments.en: «Ḥiyya bar Rav said:» This is not a case where one seeks to fulfill his obligation by responding amen; rather, it is a case «where he did not eat with them» yet still wishes to answer amen to their blessing. «And so Rav Naḥman said» that «Rabba bar Avuh said:» It is a case «where he did not eat with them.» The Gemara relates: «Rav said to his son, Ḥiyya: My son, seize» the opportunity «and recite a blessing» quickly. «And similarly Rav Huna said to his son, Rabba, seize» the opportunity «and recite a blessing.»

segments.he: לְמֵימְרָא דִּמְבָרֵךְ עֲדִיף מִמַּאן דְּעָנֵי ״אָמֵן״? וְהָתַנְיָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: גָּדוֹל הָעוֹנֶה ״אָמֵן״ יוֹתֵר מִן הַמְבָרֵךְ.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «Is that to say that one who recites a blessing is preferable to one who answers amen? Wasn’t it taught» in a baraita that «Rabbi Yosei says:» The reward of «the one who answers amen is greater than» the reward of «the one who recites the blessing?»

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי נְהוֹרַאי: הַשָּׁמַיִם, כֵּן הוּא. תִּדַּע — שֶׁהֲרֵי גּוּלְיָירִין יוֹרְדִין וּמִתְגָּרִין בַּמִּלְחָמָה, וְגִבּוֹרִים יוֹרְדִין וּמְנַצְּחִין!
segments.en: «Rabbi Nehorai said to him: By Heavens,» an oath in the name of God, «it is so. Know» that this is true, «as the military assistants [gulyarin] descend to the» battlefield «and initiate the war» and «the mighty descend and prevail.» The amen that follows a blessing is compared to the mighty who join the war after the assistants, illustrating that answering amen is more significant than reciting the initial blessing.

segments.he: תַּנָּאֵי הִיא. דְּתַנְיָא: אֶחָד הַמְבָרֵךְ וְאֶחָד הָעוֹנֶה ״אָמֵן״ בַּמַּשְׁמָע, אֶלָּא שֶׁמְּמַהֲרִין לַמְבָרֵךְ יוֹתֵר מִן הָעוֹנֶה אָמֵן.
segments.en: The Gemara responds: This is subject to «a tannaitic dispute, as it was taught» in a baraita: «Both the one who recites a blessing and the one who answers» amen «are included» among those who “stand up and bless” (Nehemiah 9:5), but «they hurry to» reward, i.e., «the one who recites the blessing, more than» they hurry to reward, i.e., «the one who answers amen.»

segments.he: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ שְׁמוּאֵל מֵרַב: מַהוּ לַעֲנוֹת ״אָמֵן״ אַחַר תִּינוֹקוֹת שֶׁל בֵּית רַבָּן? אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אַחַר הַכֹּל עוֹנִין אָמֵן, חוּץ מִתִּינוֹקוֹת שֶׁל בֵּית רַבָּן, הוֹאִיל וּלְהִתְלַמֵּד עֲשׂוּיִין. וְהָנֵי מִילֵּי בִּדְלָא עִידָּן מִפְטְרַיְיהוּ, אֲבָל בְּעִידָּן מִפְטְרַיְיהוּ — עוֹנִין.
segments.en: «Shmuel raised a dilemma before Rav: What is» the halakha with regard to «answering amen after» the blessings of «schoolchildren?» Rav «said to him: One answers amen following everyone» whom we hear recite a blessing, «except for schoolchildren, as they» recite blessings merely in order «to learn» them, not as expressions of thanksgiving. «This applies» specifically «at a time when they are not fulfilling their obligation» with the recitation of the blessing, but are simply learning. «However, at a time when they are fulfilling their obligation» through the recitation of a blessing, «one answers» amen after their blessing.

segments.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שֶׁמֶן מְעַכֵּב אֶת הַבְּרָכָה, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי זִילַאי. רַבִּי זִיוַאי אוֹמֵר: אֵינוֹ מְעַכֵּב. רַב אַחָא אוֹמֵר: שֶׁמֶן טוֹב מְעַכֵּב. רַבִּי זוּהֲמַאי אוֹמֵר: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁמְּזֹוהָם פָּסוּל לַעֲבוֹדָה, כָּךְ יָדַיִם מְזוֹהָמוֹת פְּסוּלוֹת לִבְרָכָה.
segments.en: «The Sages taught» in a baraita: If one does not have «oil» to spread on and cleanse his hands after eating, this «prevents» him from reciting «the» Grace after Meals «blessing;» this is «the statement of Rabbi Zilai. Rabbi Zivai says:» Lack of that «oil does not prevent one» from reciting Grace after Meals. «Rav Aḥa says:» Lack of «fine oil prevents one» from reciting Grace after Meals. One must wait until he rubs oil on his hands. «Rav Zuhamai says: Just as one who is filthy is unfit for Temple service, so too are filthy hands unfit for» reciting «the» Grace after Meals «blessing.»

segments.he: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: אֲנָא לָא זִילַאי וְלָא זִיוַאי וְלָא זוּהֲמַאי יָדַעְנָא אֶלָּא מַתְנִיתָא יָדַעְנָא. דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב וְאָמְרִי לַהּ בְּמַתְנִיתָא תָּנָא: ״וְהִתְקַדִּשְׁתֶּם״ אֵלּוּ מַיִם רִאשׁוֹנִים, ״וִהְיִיתֶם קְדֹשִׁים״ אֵלּוּ מַיִם אַחֲרוֹנִים, ״כִּי קָדוֹשׁ״ — זֶה שֶׁמֶן, ״אֲנִי ה׳ אֱלֹהֵיכֶם״ — זוֹ בְּרָכָה.
segments.en: «Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said» of this: «I do not know of Zilai or Zivai or Zuhamai; rather, I know a baraita, as Rav Yehuda said» that «Rav said, and some say» that it was «taught in a baraita:» It is stated: “And you shall sanctify yourselves, and you shall be holy, for holy am I, the Lord your God” (Leviticus 20:26). With regard to this verse, the Sages said: «And you shall sanctify yourselves, these are the first waters» with which one washes his hands before the meal; «and you shall be holy, these are the final waters; for holy, this is oil» which one spreads on his hands; «am I, the Lord your God, this is» the Grace after Meals «blessing.»

moves.cueHe: למימרא דישראל אף על גב דלא שמע כולה ברכה עונה?
moves.summary: reads out of the preceding mishna that a Jew answers amen even without hearing the whole blessing
moves.about: that a Jew answers amen to a blessing even though he did not hear the whole of it

moves.cueHe: וכי לא שמע היכי נפיק?
moves.summary: objects that one who did not hear the blessing cannot have discharged his obligation
moves.about: how one who did not hear the whole blessing can discharge his obligation by answering amen

moves.cueHe: אמר חייא בר רב: בשלא אכל עמהן
moves.summary: the case is one who did not eat with them, so he has no obligation to discharge
moves.about: the mishna speaks of one who did not eat with the company and so has no obligation to discharge by his amen

moves.cueHe: וכן אמר רב נחמן אמר רבה בר אבוה
moves.summary: the same answer is transmitted from Rabba bar Avuh
moves.about: the same resolution — the mishna's case is one who did not eat with the company

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה רב לחייא בריה: ברי, חטוף ובריך
moves.summary: Rav tells his son to seize the blessing for himself
moves.about: urging his son to seize the opportunity and recite the blessing himself rather than answer amen

moves.cueHe: וכן אמר רב הונא לרבה בריה: חטוף ובריך
moves.summary: Rav Huna says the same to his son
moves.about: the same instruction to his son — seize the opportunity and recite the blessing

moves.cueHe: למימרא דמברך עדיף ממאן דעני אמן?
moves.summary: infers from those instructions that reciting the blessing outranks answering amen
moves.about: that Rav's instruction implies the one who recites the blessing is preferable to the one who answers amen

moves.cueHe: והתניא רבי יוסי אומר: גדול העונה אמן יותר מן המברך
moves.summary: brings Rabbi Yosei's baraita, which ranks the answerer higher
moves.about: whether the one who recites the blessing or the one who answers amen is the greater

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה רבי נהוראי: השמים, כן הוא
moves.summary: Rabbi Nehorai swears that it is indeed so
moves.about: affirming under oath that answering amen is the greater act, proved by the analogy of the auxiliaries who open the battle and the warriors who win it

moves.cueHe: תדע — שהרי גוליירין יורדין ומתגרין במלחמה
moves.summary: proves it from the auxiliaries who open the battle and the warriors who win it

moves.cueHe: תנאי היא
moves.summary: answers that the ranking is itself disputed among tannaim
moves.about: whether the blesser or the amen-answerer is greater is itself a dispute between tannaim, so Rav need not accord with Rabbi Yosei

moves.cueHe: דתניא
moves.summary: cites the baraita that hurries reward to the one who blesses
moves.about: a baraita holding that both are included but reward is hurried to the one who blesses

moves.cueHe: בעא מיניה שמואל מרב: מהו לענות אמן אחר תינוקות של בית רבן?
moves.summary: asks Rav whether one answers amen after schoolchildren
moves.about: whether one answers amen after the blessings of schoolchildren

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה: אחר הכל עונין אמן, חוץ מתינוקות של בית רבן
moves.summary: one answers after everyone but schoolchildren, whose blessings are exercises
moves.about: one answers amen after everyone except schoolchildren, since their blessings are recited only in order to learn

moves.cueHe: והני מילי בדלא עידן מפטרייהו
moves.summary: limits the exclusion to when the children are not discharging an obligation
moves.about: Rav's exclusion of schoolchildren holds only when they are not discharging an obligation; when they are, one does answer

moves.cueHe: תנו רבנן
moves.summary: opens a baraita on what is indispensable to Grace after Meals
moves.about: a baraita disputing whether oil is indispensable to the Grace after Meals blessing

moves.cueHe: שמן מעכב את הברכה, דברי רבי זילאי
moves.summary: oil is indispensable to the blessing
moves.about: whether the absence of oil prevents one from reciting Grace after Meals

moves.cueHe: רבי זיואי אומר: אינו מעכב
moves.summary: oil is not indispensable
moves.about: whether oil in general or only fine oil is what prevents the blessing when lacking

moves.cueHe: רב אחא אומר: שמן טוב מעכב
moves.summary: only fine oil is indispensable

moves.cueHe: רבי זוהמאי אומר: כשם שמזוהם פסול לעבודה
moves.summary: filthy hands are unfit for the blessing as a filthy priest is for Temple service

moves.cueHe: אמר רב נחמן בר יצחק: אנא לא זילאי ולא זיואי ולא זוהמאי ידענא
moves.summary: disowns those tradents and says he knows only a taught baraita
moves.about: the derivation of first waters, final waters, oil and the blessing from Leviticus 20:26

moves.cueHe: דאמר רב יהודה אמר רב
moves.summary: expounds Leviticus 20:26 as first waters, final waters, oil and the blessing
moves.about: the verse whose four clauses yield first waters, final waters, oil and the blessing
